title: IO token sharding + ephemeral copy-pools to reduce host thread contention
creator: Priya Kothari
description: Investigate and implement a strategy that shards incoming token work across lightweight IO 'lanes' and uses ephemeral GPU staging copy-pools to eliminate global mutex contention in the host-side threadpool. Goal: reduce end-to-end prefill+decode p99 latency by 15-30% for mixed short/long sequence workloads and shrink CPU utilization spikes that cause tail latency degradation.
background_and_motivation: Recent load tests showed recurring CPU scheduling storms when multiple concurrent prefill streams triggered host staging allocations and synchronous memcpy paths. Current threadpool uses global queues and coarse-grained staging arenas that cause cross-core contention and repeated memcopy fan-out. This ticket explores a two-pronged approach: 1) token-level IO sharding to route work to dedicated worker lanes with per-lane queues, and 2) ephemeral pinned-buffer copy-pools that are leased to a worker for batches and returned to the pool to avoid repeated allocation/eviction noise.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Sharding granularity: shard by request source (socket/connection) vs by token age; chosen: hybrid heuristic that starts by connection affinity and falls back to token-size hashing to keep long-running streams steady.
- Copy pool sizing: small per-NUMA pools vs global pool; chosen: per-NUMA ephemeral pools sized by active GPU memory budget to minimize cross-node DMA.
- Locking strategy: per-lane lock-free MPSC queues with CAS-based admission to reduce wakeups; fallback to spinlock when queue saturated.
- Kernel interaction: expose per-lane affinity hints to kernel selector so that prefills with large KV caches prefer kernels that favor streaming attention kernels. This adds metadata on dispatch path but avoids runtime scans for affinity.
implementation_notes: 1) Introduce lane-allocator component in host runtime that maps incoming requests to lane ids. 2) Implement per-lane MPSC queue using ringlet buffer and 64B padded slots to avoid false sharing. 3) Ephemeral copy-pool: pre-allocate pinned buffers per NUMA node, each buffer tagged with last-used timestamp and a lease counter. 4) Worker lifecycle: worker leases a buffer for a microbatch, performs device copy using async DMA, then returns buffer. 5) Integrate with existing kernel dispatcher by adding optional hint header: {'lane_id','numa_node','expected_seq_len'}. 6) Metrics: track per-lane queue length, lease hit-rate, mean buffer reuse cycles, and per-lane p99 latency.
acceptance_criteria: Per-lane p99 prefill+decode latency reduced by >= 15% in mixed load benchmark (50% short seq(32), 50% long seq(2048)) compared to baseline
CPU host-side scheduling spikes (measured as runnable threads > threshold) reduced by >= 40% at peak QPS
Memcopy allocation churn (number of allocations/sec for pinned buffers) dropped by >= 80%
No regression in correctness for KV cache reuse; end-to-end generation outputs match control within expected nondeterminism
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial ticket created after postmortem of 2025-02-10 spike. Collected traces and flame graphs. Assigned to Miguel.
2025-02-18: Prototype of lane allocator with 4 lanes checked in under feature flag. Microbench harness added to repro scheduling spike locally.
2025-02-22: Ephemeral copy-pool prototype: per-NUMA pre-allocated pinned buffers implemented. Observed 60% reduction in allocation churn in local perf tests.

2025-02-26: Integrated lane hints into kernel selector; small patch to kernel hint parser merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231). Noted slight increase in dispatch path overhead (~0.4us).
2025-03-01: End-to-end mixed workload run on staging: p99 improved ~18%, CPU spikes reduced ~45%. Some tail jitter remains for pathological request interleavings. Added telemetry for lane imbalance.
2025-03-03: Rolling canary to 5% of traffic with feature flag on dedicated host; monitoring thresholds set. Preparing follow-up work to handle lane steal and dynamic re-sharding.
risks_and_mitigation: Lane imbalance: if one lane becomes hot it can starve others. Mitigation: implement periodic rehashing and lane steal protocol where idle workers can pull from busiest lane after threshold.
Pinned buffer exhaustion: under transient burst we may run out of buffers causing blocking; mitigation: fallback to queued async alloc path with backpressure signal to admission controller.
Correctness regressions with KV cache pointer lifetimes when using ephemeral buffers: mitigation: extend buffer lease semantics until GPU ack confirmed and add assert-in-debug builds.
Increased dispatcher metadata length: small perf hit; mitigation: pack hints into 64-bit header and only enable when lane-mode is active.
Cross-NUMA copy penalties: ensure copy-pools allocated per-NUMA and workers bound by affinity when possible.
